method: Actual original PNG opened separately at its original resolution before authoring any fig70 spec.
sourceFacts: One unframed cross-sectional drawing, not multiple time stages.
A tall narrow film strip extends upward from a single circular solid-wire cross-section below. The strip has two side/interface outlines and a top edge.
Two upward force arrows originate at the upper part of the wire, one alongside each film interface; both are labelled F with vector marks in the source.
One external-resultant force arrow extends downward from the bottom of the wire cross-section and is labelled F1 with a vector mark.
The wire cross-section is filled with diagonal historical hatching. Film stippling and wire hatching are material indications, not countable particles, interface subdivisions or calibration ticks.
The source has no printed AB label in this cross-section, no measured wire diameter or film thickness, and no numbered scale or force magnitude beyond the symbolic F/F1 labels.
sourceIdentity: Complete current n46 prose identifies F as the force of one of the two soap-film interfaces and F1 as spring-force-plus-weight resultant. This is the same movable wire AB shown in fig69.
regularization: Smooth schematic interface lines, circular wire contour and a light solid wire fill replace raster hatching. A modern AB label may identify the same wire, explicitly as a text-bound addition. Arrow lengths, thickness and coordinates are illustrative only, not source measurements.
constructionPolicy: Every coordinate point is a hidden construction anchor. The circular wire is the only visible closed round object; no anchor dots or new particles may appear.
